short: Led the last great Welsh revolt and held a parliament as an uncrowned prince.
full:
Owain Glyndwr was a Welsh landowner of princely descent, with legal training and English military service behind him, when a property dispute with a neighbouring lord went unheard at Westminster. On 16 September 1400 his followers proclaimed him Prince of Wales, and a local quarrel became a national revolt.

By 1404 he held Harlech and Aberystwyth, had summoned a parliament at Machynlleth, had sought recognition from the French, and had set out a programme including an independent Welsh church and two universities. He allied with the Percys and Edmund Mortimer, and the Tripartite Indenture proposed dividing England and Wales between them. Henry of Monmouth, the future Henry V, ground the revolt down from 1405 by blockade and the recapture of the castles, and Aberystwyth and Harlech fell in 1408-09. Glyndwr was never captured or betrayed, and disappeared from the record around 1415.
